scenarios.title: The Fan's Memory
scenarios.text: A fan shows you a ticket stub from your first pro game, kept in a plastic sleeve for years. She was eleven at the time, and now she's brought her own kid, who is wearing your number.

choices.label: Sign the stub
choices.result: A signature on the stub, and another on the kid's jersey, with both their names. She cries a little, and the kid asks why, and she tries to explain it.

choices.label: Invite them to practice
choices.result: A practice pass for both of them, and a hold for the kid on the sideline. The kid tells everyone at school, and the mother sends you a letter that you keep.

choices.label: Ask about the game
choices.result: Questions about that first game: where she sat, what she remembers, what you looked like. Her memory is better than yours, and you hear your own career from the outside.

scenarios.title: The Kicker's Union
scenarios.text: You've been talking with a few kickers and punters about health after football: hips, knees, heads, the things nobody measures. Someone suggests starting a group, and everyone looks at you.

choices.label: Start the group
choices.result: A group chat, then a monthly call, then a doctor who agrees to join. By the end of the season forty specialists are on it, sharing what nobody told them.

choices.label: Bring it to the union
choices.result: The idea, brought to the players' union with a short proposal. It moves slowly, the way unions do, and a year later it becomes a real program.

choices.label: Ask someone younger to lead
choices.result: A younger punter with more energy, asked to lead it while you help. She's brilliant at it, and you're glad you stepped back.

choices.label: Write the honesty rules
choices.result: Rules for the group about money and sponsors, because you saw in college what happens when nobody writes them. The doctors trust the group because of it.
choices.lock_text: having reported a runner in college
